description:

Choosing BDC as your employer
means working in a healthy, inclusive, and skilled workplace that puts forward the best conditions to bring together unique teams where employees are empowered to act. It also means being at the centre of ambitious economic and financial projects to see further and to do things differently, to fuel the success of Canadian entrepreneurs.

POSITION OVERVIEW
As a Senior Business Advisor, Strategy within BDC Advisory Services, you act as a senior strategic advisor to entrepreneurs and executive teams at pivotal moments of growth, transformation, and ownership transition. BDC is the only bank dedicated exclusively to Canadian entrepreneurs, and your work directly supports the long‑term success of small and medium‑sized businesses across Canada.
This position resides in Advisory Services (management consulting) and will serve Canadian Small and Medium Entrepreneurs through our consulting mandates. This is not a Financing role. The ideal candidate will have strong business strategy consulting experience with M&A (mergers and acquisitions) and PMI (post-merger integration) experience. The ideal candidate will have a vision for the future of business in an AI driven world and will have supported the consulting sales cycle and management of a portfolio of projects delivered by consultants.
CHALLENGES TO BE MET
Lead complex, high‑impact advisory mandates for entrepreneurs and senior leadership teams, focused on enterprise‑level strategic planning, growth acceleration, organizational effectiveness, and leadership decision‑making within SME and mid‑market environments.
Maintain full accountability for mandate outcomes across multiple concurrent engagements, ensuring delivery excellence related to scope, budget, timelines, risk management, and quality of deliverables.
Act as a trusted senior advisor during periods of ambiguity, transformation, and change, applying market insight, competitive analysis, and practical experience to guide high‑stakes decisions.
Contribute to the evolution of the Strategy Centre of Expertise by developing, refining, and scaling advisory solutions, tools, and methodologies aligned with emerging client needs and market trends.
Support business development and revenue growth by partnering with senior client managers on complex sales cycles, including executive‑level diagnostics, value articulation, and proposal development.
Enable strong internal collaboration by connecting advisors, delivery teams, and relationship managers, ensuring continuity of client strategy and effective knowledge transfer across engagements.
Represent BDC Advisory Services externally through thought leadership, content development, speaking engagements, and participation in targeted events that promote Business and Organizational Capabilities solutions. At BDC, we think and act differently, and we value inclusion, equity, and authenticity—you can be yourself at work while making a tangible impact on Canadian businesses.
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
Required Qualifications (Must‑Have)
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Management, Strategy, or a related discipline.
Minimum
10 years of progressive experience
in a consulting environment, with senior responsibility for:
Enterprise‑level strategic planning
Executive advisory to entrepreneurs and senior management teams
Leading complex, customized consulting mandates
Demonstrated experience advising SMEs or mid‑market organizations.

business strategy consulting
, including

and

Executive‑level communication and presentation skills, with credibility to influence senior stakeholders and support high‑stakes advisory and sales conversations.

title: Analyst, Secondaries
description:
Purpose. Performance. People.
Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.
With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide.
For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute
to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success.
The Role
As an Analyst, Secondaries, you will support the evaluation and execution of private equity secondary investments across both LP and GP-led transactions. Working closely with the Secondaries team, you will conduct investment research, build financial models, participate in due diligence, and help monitor portfolio investments while contributing to investment recommendations and portfolio management activities.
The Team
The Secondaries group is part of CPP Investments' Private Equity department and invests directly in the private equity market through both LP and GP-led secondaries. The team leverages CPP Investments' scale, extensive market access, longstanding GP relationships, and established track record to identify and execute compelling investment opportunities.
Accountabilities
Conduct industry, market, and company research to support investment analysis and due diligence.
Develop and maintain financial models and perform valuation analysis to evaluate investment opportunities.
Participate in due diligence activities, including meetings with external stakeholders and analysis of investment opportunities.
Prepare investment memoranda, analytical reviews, and recommendations in collaboration with the deal team.
Present analysis during investment discussions and contribute to transaction-related Q&A sessions.
Monitor the financial performance and risk profile of portfolio investments, updating models and analytical tools as required.
Support multiple transaction teams simultaneously while contributing to investment execution and portfolio management.
What You Bring
Undergraduate degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related field.
Up to 3 years of relevant experience in secondaries or private equity, investment banking, consulting, or a related field.
CFA designation or progress toward the CFA program is considered an asset.
Strong financial modelling, valuation, research, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively in a team environment.
Willingness to be based in Toronto and travel as required.
You are motivated to contribute to something larger than yourself, approach complex challenges with rigor, and hold yourself to
high standards in a collaborative, performance-driven environment.
We provide colleagues with cutting-edge AI tools, dedicated learning time, and practical support to help them deliver with greater impact.
Inclusion & Accessibility
CPP Investments is committed to
equitable access to employment and building a workforce that reflects diverse talent and perspectives. If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.
Attention: Protect Yourself from Fraud
CPP Investments is committed to a secure and transparent recruitment process. We will never ask candidates for payment or financial information at any stage of hiring. All legitimate opportunities are posted on our careers page, and communications will come from our applicant tracking system, Workday.
CPP Investments may use AI tools to help screen and assess applicants by analyzing resumes and applications for relevant skills and experience. These tools support, but do not replace, human decision-making.

title: Senior Manager, L&H Insurance Policy
employer: Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario (FSRA)
description:
At FSRA, our vision is to ensure financial safety, fairness, and choice for Ontarians. As a financial services regulator, we’re passionate about protecting consumers. Our principles-based approach means we can quickly and effectively respond to the changing needs of consumers and the industry.
Our team combines industry expertise with commitment to public service. We attract individuals who are interested in
meaningful work and who measure success through outcomes, not inputs.
At FSRA, we invest in the personal and professional growth of our team.  We offer a competitive compensation package that includes an
employer-matched
defined benefit pension plan
, and a comprehensive and competitive benefits plan. We prioritize learning and development, wellbeing, diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging, and community giving.
Join FSRA and help us shape the future of regulation for generations to come!
Job Description:
Salary Range - $106,462 -$156,462
(salary will be determined based on the successful candidate's skills, experience and qualifications)
PURPOSE OF POSITION
To manage the research, analysis, design, development and delivery of regulatory guidance and rules in an assigned sector (life & health insurance, mortgage brokers, financial planners/advisors) in support of overall Policy department strategies
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Oversees the planning, design, development and delivery of the FSRA policy agenda and principles-based, risk-focused, regulatory framework
Provides policy expertise and advice to FSRA management and staff in response to a range of Policy issues impacting the achievement of department directions and FSRA mandate; providing evidence-based recommendations for problem resolution and improvement to methods to deliver programs or services
As part of the management team, supports FSRA leadership in formulating strategy and developing tactics and provides leadership in executing programs or services to deliver on strategy and tactics.
Works in collaboration with colleagues on section / department / FSRA strategic priorities.
Manages the research, environmental scans, monitoring, analysis and assessment of a broad range of issues, trends and developments, which affect the development of FSRA policies and programs, including evidence-based research and data provided by various sources as well as policies and procedures related to the interpretation and application of relevant legislation.
Manages the delivery of Policy initiatives for an assigned sector (e.g., Life & Health Insurance, Mortgage Brokers, Financial Planners/Advisors) related to industry Market Conduct; ensuring consistency with overall Policy Development performance measures, standards and best practices, and integration with overall FSRA directions.
Delivers policy research and analysis projects/initiatives to support policy development related to the regulation of financial service sectors in Ontario and related to industry market conduct.
Leads the development and oversight of plans and policies, including operational processes and procedures, policy development/review models, processes and methodologies and standards, to meet the overall operational plans and priorities of the section or department.
Leads consultations and partnership projects with internal and external stakeholders for the development, review and analysis of new/revised legislation, regulations and policies, including but not limited to engagement with FSRA’s Consumer Advisory Panel, Stakeholder Advisory Committees, Technical Advisory Committees and any other relevant organizations.
Manages and coordinates consultations with other Canadian/international jurisdictions to research/analyze regulatory policy approaches and trends and to facilitate an integrated approach to policy/regulation applications across related jurisdictions.
Develops and manages relationships and consultation with stakeholders impacted by unit programs and operations to discuss and clarify program or service-related issues and needs.
Manages the unit and its staff to support an environment and culture of service excellence which respects diversity, encourages all employees to work together to achieve results and contribute to a healthy, rewarding and productive working environment where personal and team accountability are key to meeting the mandate of FSRA.
Builds a strong team including hiring, orientation, training and coaching of staff, determination of performance standards, conduct of performance reviews and management of performance and employee relations matters.
Works with the Director in operational planning, development and reporting on performance metrics, program effectiveness, risks and impacts related to unit, section and department matters. Recommends approval of financial transactions to the Director.
Supports critical change and a collaborative, forward thinking culture within the unit, and works with others to achieve this across the section or department.
Promotes and supports the implementation of innovation and continuous improvement throughout the unit and section or department.
Leads and/or participates in projects within the section/department to represent the unit’s interests in program or service decision making.
QUALIFICATIONS
Education and Experience
Postsecondary degree in finance, law, economics, public policy or related field, or equivalent experience.
6 – 8 years’ experience in planning and managing the development of policy, programs, services, initiatives in the areas of financial services, public policy and/or regulatory oversight and in interpreting legislation/regulations, design programs/services directly or on behalf of government.
Relevant industry experience preferred, with a focus on one or more of the following sectors – life and health insurance, mortgage brokers, financial planners / advisors.
Experience / expertise in leading successful consultations and partnerships with stakeholders.
Knowledge and Skills
Knowledge of government decision-making and policy development processes as well as legislative/regulatory design principles.
Skills and ability to manage and champion an effective organizational culture and vision.
Skilled in leading policy development and implementing strategies and directions or equivalent skills and experience.
Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written, to convey complex processes and policy initiatives to a broad audience and to ensure information is effectively shared.
Leadership skills to build individual and team capabilities through direction, collaboration, feedback, and coaching, including managing performance, fostering an inclusive work environment, and handling human resources matters.
Expertise in leading complex, policy projects from initiation to completion, managing competing priorities and deadlines, monitoring progress, and using project management methodologies.
Proven experience in leading and implementing major policy initiatives, anticipating impacts, managing resistance, and driving innovation.
Strong political acuity, tact, and sound judgement to recognize and manage complex, sensitive, and high-profile policy related issues and provide appropriate strategic and risk management advice to senior executives.
Proven ability to build and maintain strong relationships with diverse internal and external stakeholders, partners to build consensus and gain support for policy initiatives.

title: Director, Capital Markets and Regulatory Legal
description:
At IMCO, our talent is among the best! IMCO offers a uniquely stimulating and rewarding environment where you can help build and drive organizational transformation, all while seeking to challenge yourself, learn, and grow your career.
Our culture is built on collaboration and passion, with a shared commitment to delivering lasting value to the clients we serve. Located in downtown Toronto, our vision is to be the partner of choice for Ontario’s public sector funds and to build a high-performing, value-driven asset management firm.
This job posting is for an existing vacancy. If you are ready to deliver best-in-class service and join a collaborative, motivated and fun team of professionals, IMCO offers the opportunity to do impactful work and broaden your expertise.
If you’re looking to use your expertise to drive strategic outcomes, we’d love to hear from you.
‎
As a key member of our legal team, the Director, Legal - Capital Markets and Regulatory, provides legal and transactional support for IMCO’s capital markets activities, including derivatives, and is responsible for supporting and advising on a wide range of investment and enterprise regulatory matters. Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Legal, this role will collaborate with partners across various departments within the organization as well as engage with external counsel and other stakeholders outside the organization.
As a member of our team, you will be responsible for:
Providing legal advice and support on a wide range of legal documentation, including
derivative contracts, trading agreements, and brokerage agreements.
Providing legal advice and support on a broad range of regulatory matters, including securities regulations, compliance, filing and disclosure requirements, trading activities, and sustainable investing.
Staying apprised of, reviewing and analysing regulatory developments and changes and advising internal stakeholders of their impact on IMCO’s investments and operations.
Supporting Know-Your-Client (KYC) and Anti-Money-Laundering (AML) processes related to onboarding of counterparties.
Collaborating with internal stakeholders, including Front Office, Compliance, and Risk, to develop and implement policies, procedures and best practices to support compliance with both investment and enterprise regulatory requirements and internal controls.
Supporting strategic projects for the organization, including managing cross-functional stakeholders.
Acting as a trusted advisor to business units to assess and mitigate various legal risks.
What you need to succeed:
6+ years post-call experience gained at a major law firm or as in house counsel practicing securities regulatory law or derivatives law.
Legal expertise in derivative transactions is a must.
Knowledge of securities regulation would be an asset.
Law degree (J.D. or LL.B.) from an accredited law school; MBA or CFA designation would be an asset.
Call to the Ontario Bar and member in good standing with the Law Society of Upper Canada.
Excellent legal and business judgment.
Excellent written and oral communication and negotiation skills, with the ability to translate technical concepts and conclusions into a language applicable to the targeted audience.
Well-established interpersonal relationship-building skills and an ability to work both independently and collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders.
Ability and desire to ‘hit the ground running’.
Highly motivated team player with a proven ability to manage several different priorities at one time, including under tight timelines.
‎
We thank all applicants for their interest. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.
Our hybrid work model prioritizes an office-first approach, encouraging employees to make the most of our collaborative workspace at 16 York Street, Suite 2400, Toronto, ON M5J 0E6. This welcoming environment fosters teamwork, connection, and professional growth. While flexibility remains a key component of our model, we believe that regular in-office engagement enhances productivity and strengthens our culture. Our approach supports a fulfilling lifestyle that balances professional ambition with personal wellbeing.
IMCO is committed to providing accommodation for people with disabilities throughout the recruitment process. If you require support, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools may be used to support parts of our recruitment process, such as screening and assessments. However, all hiring decisions are made by our recruitment team. Candidates being considered for this position will be required to undergo background screening.

We're seeking a strategic and technically strong Financial Analyst to join our Reporting & Analysis team. This role offers a unique opportunity to apply deep International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) expertise to complex accounting matters, external financial reporting, and accounting policy development. If you enjoy acting as an internal accounting advisor, providing IFRS advisory services to business partners, assessing the accounting implications of significant transactions and emerging business initiatives, developing accounting policies, and preparing technical accounting memoranda and position papers, we want to hear from you.
Reporting to the Director, Reporting & Analysis, the Financial Analyst will play a key role in the preparation of IFRS-compliant financial statements and disclosures, accounting policy development, technical accounting research, and audit support activities for the LCBO. The successful candidate will serve as a trusted advisor on complex accounting and financial reporting matters, providing guidance on the application of IFRS while supporting the organization's commitment to accurate, transparent, and high-quality financial reporting.
If you thrive in a collaborative environment, enjoy interpreting and applying accounting standards to real-world business scenarios, and have a proven ability to communicate complex technical accounting matters to a broad range of stakeholders, this is an exceptional opportunity to make a meaningful impact.
About the Role
Prepare reports, analysis and information required by various stakeholder including the LCBO business partners, internal auditors and the Provincial auditors for the year end audit.
Research, interpret, and apply IFRS requirements to complex accounting transactions and emerging business initiatives.
Act as an internal accounting policy advisor, providing IFRS guidance and advisory services to finance and business stakeholders.
Prepare technical accounting memoranda, accounting position papers, and recommendations for management related to significant accounting matters.
Assess the impact of new and amended accounting standards and support implementation initiatives across the organization.
Coordinate and support internal and external year-end audit activities, including responding to audit inquiries and documenting accounting positions.
Support period-end, quarterly, year-end close and reporting cycles, including journal entries, variance analysis and meaningful financial insights for senior management.
Assist with ad hoc projects and strategic initiatives related to financial reporting, technical accounting, and finance transformation.
About You
Post-secondary education in financial or business field and/or equivalent working experience.
Chartered Professional Accounting designation and CA are preferred.
Demonstrated experience in dealing with and applying IFRS/IASs.
External reporting experience in Retail field area, with the ability to draft external financial statement in accordance with IFRS standards.
Experience researching accounting issues and preparing technical accounting memos, position papers, and policy documentation.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint and Power BI, with strong working knowledge of SAP S/4 HANA and SAP Fiori considered strong assets.
Strong Financial modelling skills and knowledge working with financial reporting systems, in support of periodic commentary and presentation for management decision support.
Strong understanding of internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR).
Ability to handle many tasks and competing priorities with proficiency to employ financial analysis, reporting techniques and always be best in class.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, along with proven track record to effectively work in a team environment.
Ability to quickly adapt to change and build and sustain business relationships.

a Defined Benefit Pension

title: Tissue Coordinator
description:
À Santé Ontario, nous sommes résolus à bâtir une solide culture organisationnelle qui unifie et responsabilise tous les membres de notre équipe à travers la province. Notre vision est qu'ensemble, nous serons des responsables en matière de santé et de bien-être pour tous. Notre mission est d'interconnecter le système de santé afin de favoriser l'amélioration et l'équité des résultats, des expériences et de la valeur en matière de santé. Notre façon de travailler ensemble se reflète dans nos cinq valeurs, l'intégrité, l'inspiration, la ténacité, l'humilité et l'attention.
Envie de donner un nouveau souffle à votre carrière?  Saisissez cette opportunité!
Rattaché à :
Responsable, PRC - Tissu
Classification :
Coordonnateur des tissus
Lieu de travail :
483, rue Bay, Toronto
Calendrier :
Combinaison de quarts de travail de 12 heures en semaine et le week-end
Type d'emploi
:
à temps partiel permanent
(0.75 ETP)
Taux horaire :
de 34,13 $ à 42,65 $
Le Réseau Trillium pour le don de vie (TGLN), qui fait partie de Santé Ontario, est responsable de la coordination du don et de la transplantation d’organes et de tissus en Ontario. Notre mandat comprend la sensibilisation accrue du public à l’importance du don d’organes et de tissus, la formation des professionnels de la santé et la mise en place d’un système de don et de transplantation sûr et efficace en Ontario. En travaillant en collaboration avec nos parties prenantes et en favorisant la croissance organisationnelle et individuelle, nous valorisons l'honnêteté, la confiance, le respect et la compassion.
Nous recherchons actuellement un coordinateur de tissus
à temps partiel permanent
(0,75 ETP) très motivé (TC). Le titulaire du poste devra fournir des services professionnels liés au don de tissus d'une manière conforme à la mission et aux valeurs de TGLN. Le coordinateur des tissus finalise les procédures de sélection des donneurs, contacte les familles pour obtenir leur consentement au don, s'assure de l'acceptation des tissus par différentes banques de tissus, coordonne les activités de prélèvement et effectue un suivi auprès des familles après le don pour les tissus non prélevés ayant fait l'objet d'un consentement
Voici ce que vous allez faire :
Activités de sélection des donneurs : Évaluation de l'aptitude clinique du donneur et recueil des antécédents médicaux et sociaux en concertation avec la famille
Approche de consentement téléphonique : Contacter les familles par téléphone pour les informer du processus de don et obtenir leur consentement au don
Coordination des cas : mise à disposition de différents tissus à différentes banques en fournissant les antécédents médicaux et sociaux nécessaires du donneur, le transfert du corps, la négociation de la date et du lieu de l’intervention chirurgicale, et les services hospitaliers.
Soutien aux familles de donneurs
Chef d'équipe (lorsqu'il est désigné)
Assurance qualité
Loi sur la santé et la sécurité au travail et l’accessibilité pour les personnes handicapées de l’Ontario
Répond aux appels des hôpitaux référents reçus au Centre provincial de ressources, effectue une évaluation préliminaire des antécédents du patient et identifie toutes les options de don pertinentes;
Fournit des services de consultation en tant qu'expert en matière de don de tissus;
Évalue la consultation d'experts concernant la pertinence des tissus ou d'autres problèmes médicaux, le cas échéant
Fournit aux banques de tissus des informations complètes concernant l'adéquation des donneurs et des tissus en vue de leur prélèvement. Les informations sont fournies conformément à la législation en vigueur sur la protection de la vie privée et aux politiques de confidentialité de TGLN
Réalisation en temps opportun du bilan médico-social, généralement au moment du don, parfois à une date et une heure convenues à l'avance afin de minimiser les occasions manquées.
Il contacte le décideur suppléant en temps opportun et le recontacte si nécessaire pour obtenir son consentement au don de tissus
Apprend et applique de nouvelles techniques et stratégies d'approche
Participe à la formation continue et à la sensibilisation à l'évaluation
Assure la liaison en permanence avec le personnel sur place (c.-à-d. OTDC, professionnels de la santé et personnel de rétablissement) de l'hôpital référent pour effectuer l'évaluation des risques, le dépistage, les tests et l'évaluation de l'adéquation des tissus individuels après consentement;
Collabore avec le bureau du coroner pour faciliter le don de tissus et transmet les cas au coroner superviseur régional au cas par cas;
Obtient des privilèges chirurgicaux temporaires pour le personnel de prélèvement de tissus, lorsque cela est nécessaire, conformément aux politiques de l'hôpital référent, en veillant à ce que le processus d'accréditation soit en place au moment opportun;
Coordonne le calendrier et la confirmation de la disponibilité de la salle de réveil (OR) et de l'arrivée des équipes de prélèvement de tissus;
Transmet toutes les informations pertinentes concernant le donneur au personnel compétent en matière de prélèvement de tissus et à la banque de tissus concernée;
S'assure que le ou les services hospitaliers concernés soient contactés après le prélèvement des tissus afin d'assurer le transport rapide du corps vers la maison funéraire.
Communique et interagit avec les membres de la famille;
Informe les familles lorsque les possibilités de don ne peuvent être menées à terme malgré un consentement signé
Assume la responsabilité du travail du groupe pendant un quart de travail donné;
Priorise et attribue le travail, y compris les cas actifs de don de tissus, le suivi et la clôture des cas de référence précoce, les tâches de suivi;
Supervise l'attribution du tutorat aux nouveaux employés afin de garantir que le nouveau membre de l'équipe ait la possibilité d'apprendre et d'atteindre les objectifs d'orientation;
Diffuse un rapport de quart précis;
Assure le suivi et l'attribution des dossiers et de leur clôture avec l'équipe PRC-Tissue;
Suivi des dossiers de dons d'organes en cours et de leur statut en vue d'un don de tissus
Utilise son expérience et son jugement cliniques pour répondre aux questions relatives à la compatibilité tissulaire avant de faire intervenir le médecin responsable ou le médecin consultant;
S'assure que, lorsqu'ils ne sont pas désignés comme chef d'équipe, les TC de service sont responsables de suivre les directives du chef d'équipe.
Assure la responsabilité de la saisie en temps voulu et de l'exactitude des données dans tous les systèmes électroniques et les dossiers papier;
Assume la responsabilité de documenter et de signaler les écarts par rapport aux IPC et les plaintes;
Assume la responsabilité du respect des politiques et procédures/CPI (cliniques et administratives).
Voici ce dont vous aurez besoin pour réussir :
Formation et expérience
Un diplôme universitaire ou collégial en sciences de la santé, en sciences biologiques ou dans une discipline équivalente reconnue est requis
Une certification en banque d'yeux ou de tissus (technicien certifié en banque d'yeux (CEBT)/spécialiste certifié en banque de tissus (CTBS)), en banque de sang, en tant qu'infirmier(ère) auxiliaire autorisé(e) (IAA) ou ambulancier(ère) paramédical(e) est un atout.
Une expérience professionnelle d'au moins trois (3) ans dans le domaine du don d'organes et de tissus, des sciences de la santé ou des soins de santé, ainsi que dans la récupération et le traitement des tissus, est préférable
Une expérience dans un établissement de soins de santé ou auprès de patients et de leurs familles en période de crise est préférable
Capacité à travailler par quarts de 12 heures dans un environnement fonctionnant 24h/24 et 7j/7, incluant les jours, les nuits et les heures creuses.  De plus, il est obligatoire de travailler les week-ends et les jours fériés.
Tous les horaires de jour exigent une présence au bureau
Connaissances et compétences
Une connaissance approfondie des sciences biologiques et de la santé ainsi que des normes d'assurance qualité est un atout
Capacité à maintenir et à protéger la confidentialité des patients en tout temps, en faisant preuve de discrétion et de discernement
Aptitudes démontrées en gestion du temps, avec la capacité et la flexibilité nécessaires pour prioriser plusieurs tâches et projets dans un environnement dynamique et axé sur les résultats
Personne motivée et autonome, capable de travailler aussi bien seule qu'en équipe
Excellentes aptitudes à la communication écrite et orale
Précision et souci du détail
Solides compétences informatiques
Lieu de travail :
Toronto, On
Tous les candidats doivent être résidents de l'Ontario pour être admissibles aux postes à Ontario Health.
Santé Ontario encourage les candidatures des personnes appartenant aux Premières Nations, aux communautés métisses, inuites et autochtones en milieu urbain; des personnes francophones; des personnes noires et racisées; des personnes 2SLGBTQIA+; des personnes trans et non binaires; et des personnes en situation de handicap.
Santé Ontario est un employeur accessible et offre des mesures d’adaptation à toutes les étapes du processus d’emploi, y compris le processus de recrutement. Si vous avez besoin de mesures d’adaptation liées à un handicap pour participer au processus de recrutement, veuillez envoyer un courriel à careers@ontariohealth.ca. Un membre de l’équipe communiquera avec vous dans les 48 heures.
Tissue Coordinator
At Ontario Health, we are committed to developing a strong organizational culture that connects and inspires all team members across the province. Our vision is that together, we will be a leader in health and wellness for all. Our mission is to connect the health system to drive improved and equitable health outcomes, experiences and value. How we work together is reflected through our five values: integrity, inspiration, tenacity, humility and care
Want to make a difference in your career?  Consider this opportunity!
Reporting to:
Manager, PRC - Tissue
Classification:
Tissue Coordinator
Worksite:
483 Bay Street, Toronto
Schedule:
Combination of weekday and weekend 12 hour shifts
Employment Type
:  Permanent Part time (0.75 fte)
Rate of Pay:
$34.13 to $42.65 per hour
Trillium Gift of Life Network (TGLN), part of Ontario Health, is responsible for the coordination of organ and tissue donation and transplantation in Ontario. Our mandate includes increasing public awareness of the importance of organ and tissue donation, education of health care professionals, and ensuring a safe and effective donation and transplant system in Ontario. Working collaboratively with our stakeholders and fostering organizational and individual growth, we value honesty, trust, respect and compassion.
We are currently seeking a highly motivated permanent part time (0.75)  Tissue Coordinator (TC). The incumbent shall provide professional services related to tissue donation in a manner consistent with the mission and values of TGLN. The Tissue Coordinator completes processes for donor screening, approaches families for consent to donate, secures acceptance of tissues by various tissue banks, coordinates recovery activities, and conducts family follow up post-donation for consented non-recovered tissues
Here is what you will be doing:
Donor Screening Activities: Assessment of clinical suitability of donor and completion of medical/social history in consultation with family
Telephone Consent Approach: Engaging in telephone approach to families regarding the donation process and securing consent to donate from family members
Case Coordination: offering various tissues to various banks by providing necessary donor medical/social history, body transfer, negotiating OR time and location, and hospital services.
Donor Family Support
Team Lead (when assigned)
Quality assurance
Occupational Health and Safety/ Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act
Responds to calls from referring hospitals received in the Provincial Resource Centre, conducts a preliminary assessment of the patient’s history and identifies all relevant donation options;
Provides consultation services as an expert in matters relating to tissue donation;
Assesses expert consultation regarding tissue suitability or other medical issues as appropriate
Provides complete information to the tissue bank(s) concerning donor and tissue suitability for placement of tissues. The information is provided in a manner that complies with existing privacy legislation and TGLN confidentiality policies
Timely completion of the med-soc, usually at time of donation, occasionally at a pre-arranged date and time to minimize missed opportunities.
Approaches the substitute decision maker in a timely manner, and re-approaches when necessary to obtain consent for tissue donation
Learns and applies new techniques and strategies for approach
Participates in ongoing education and evaluation awareness
Liaises continuously with on-site personnel (ie. OTDC, health-care professionals and recovery staff) at referring hospital to complete risk assessment, screening, testing and evaluation of individual tissue suitability after consent;
Works with the coroner’s office to facilitate tissue donation and escalates cases to Regional Supervising Coroner on a case by case basis;
Obtains temporary surgical privileges for tissue recovery personnel, when necessary, in accordance with the policies of the referring hospital, ensuring compliance with the credentialing process is in place at the time;
Coordinates timing and confirmation of recovery facility (OR) availability and arrival of tissue recovery teams;
Conveys all relevant information regarding the donor to the appropriate tissue recovery personnel and relevant Tissue Bank;
Ensures relevant hospital department(s) are contacted following tissue recovery for timely transport of body to funeral home.
Communicates and engages with family members;
Informs families when donation opportunities cannot go forward despite a signed consent
Takes accountability for the work of the group during a given shift;
Prioritizes and assigns work including active tissue donation cases, early referral case follow up and closure, follow up tasks;
Oversees the assignment of preceptorship of new employees to ensure new team member is given the opportunity to learn and meet orientation objectives;
Distributes an accurate shift report;
Monitors and assigns case follow up and case closure with PRC-Tissue Team;
Tracks active organ cases and their status for tissue offering
Uses clinical experience and judgment to answer TC questions prior to involving the MOC or involving the consulting physician regarding tissue suitability;
Ensures, when not assigned Team Lead, TCs on shift are responsible for following the Team Lead’s direction.
Takes responsibility for timeliness and accuracy of data entered into all electronic systems and paper charting;
Takes responsibility for documenting and reporting variance(s) from CPI’s and complaint(s);
Takes responsibility for compliance with policies and procedures/CPIs (both Clinical and Administrative).
Here is what you will need to be successful:
Education and Experience
University degree or college diploma in health sciences, biological sciences or a recognized equivalent major is required
Certification in eye or tissue banking (Certified Eye Bank Technician (CEBT)/Certified Tissue Banking Specialist (CTBS), blood banking, as a Registered Practical Nurse (RPN) or a paramedic is an asset
Minimum of three (3) years working experience in organ and tissue donation, health sciences or health care environment, tissue recovery and processing is preferred
Experience in a healthcare setting or working with patients and their families at times of crisis is preferred
Ability to work 12 hour shifts in a 24/7 environment which includes days, nights and mid day.  In addition, there is a requirement to work weekends and statutory holidays.
All days shifts are required to work in office at 483 Bay Street
Knowledge and Skills
In-depth knowledge of biological and health sciences as well as quality assurance standards is an asset
Ability to maintain and protect patient confidentiality at all times, demonstrating use of discretion and sound judgment
Demonstrated time management skills with the ability and flexibility to prioritize multiple tasks and projects in a fast paced, results oriented environment
Motivated self-starter with the ability to work independently and collaboratively as part of a team
Demonstrated superior written and oral communication skills
Accuracy and close attention to detail
Strong computer skills

Toronto, Ontario

title: Senior Data Scientist
description:

The Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) is the statutory body responsible for regulating Ontario’s capital markets in accordance with the mandate established in the provincial Securities Act and the Commodity Futures Act. The mandate of the OSC is to provide protection to investors from unfair, improper or fraudulent practices, to foster fair, efficient and competitive capital markets and confidence in the capital markets, to foster capital formation, and to contribute to the stability of the financial system and the reduction of systemic risk. This mandate is performed through policy, operational, and enforcement activities. The OSC also contributes to national and global securities regulation development.
We offer a diverse, fair, and flexible work environment and take pride in our challenging and rewarding work.
The opportunity
Reporting to the Manager, Analytics & Technology Innovation, you will provide strategic leadership and hands-on technical expertise in advanced analytics and data science. You will develop cloud-based analytics products, help shape the OSC’s analytics roadmap, and guide technical staff while collaborating with stakeholders across the organization.
This is an opportunity for an experienced data science professional who combines deep technical capability with strong business judgment, clear communication, and an understanding of capital markets or regulatory environments.
What you will do
Lead the design and delivery of advanced analytics and data science solutions for divisions across the OSC.
Mine, clean, analyze and synthesize large structured and unstructured data sets into useful data products and insights.
Architect, prototype, test and deliver complex cloud-based analytics solutions that demonstrate business value quickly.
Lead multiple analytics projects in parallel, managing deliverables, timelines, service commitments and stakeholder expectations.
Collaborate with stakeholders to clarify needs, onboard and refine data, and translate abstract concepts into tangible deliverables.
Apply Python, artificial intelligence, natural language processing and text mining to solve complex business problems.
Contribute to analytics standards, methodologies, controls and best practices, including code review, quality assurance and knowledge sharing.
Guide and mentor data science team staff, coordinate task-level work, monitor progress and support capability development.
Build training materials and educate OSC staff on new analytics processes and products.
Participate in Agile ceremonies, including sprint planning, backlog refinement, stakeholder demonstrations and daily scrums.
What you bring
Bachelor's degree in mathematics, computer science, computer engineering, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. A master's degree is considered an asset.
At least five years of relevant experience in data science, advanced analytics or application development.
Experience working in capital markets, a regulatory environment or a financial setting.
Advanced proficiency with Python and experience with analytics or development technologies such as R, Scala, PySpark, Angular or React JS.
Strong experience delivering complex data science solutions using open-source tools and Microsoft Azure services.
Expertise in natural language processing, text mining, artificial intelligence, and structured and unstructured big data.
The ability to assess emerging AI developments and identify practical applications for the organization.
Excellent critical thinking, analytical, decision-making and problem-solving skills.
The ability to communicate complex technical and business concepts clearly to diverse audiences at all levels.
Strong stakeholder relationship, negotiation, organization and prioritization skills, with a results-oriented approach.
Experience mentoring junior staff and helping build stronger technical teams.
Grow your career and make a difference working at the OSC.

title: Business & Data Analyst
employer: Public Health Ontario (Ontario Agency for Health Protection and Promotion)
description:
Business & Data Analyst
Location: Toronto-661 University
Department: Planning, Reporting & Compliance
This posting is to fill a current vacancy.
The Role:
To provide advanced data analytics, validation, and visualization support to Finance-led special projects. This role focuses on transforming clinical, operational, and financial datasets into clear, actionable insights to support executive decision-making, strategic planning, and operational improvement initiatives.
Key
Responsibilities-
Data Integration & Management: Extract, integrate, and structure complex clinical, operational, and financial datasets from multiple systems.
Data Validation & Governance: Lead data quality assessment, validation, and reconciliation to ensure reliable inputs for executive reporting.
Advanced Analysis & Insight Generation: Independently analyze data to identify trends, drivers, and opportunities related to cost, performance, and operational efficiency.
Executive Visualization & Storytelling: Develop dashboards and visual outputs (e.g., Power BI) and translate insights into clear, actionable recommendations for senior leadership.
Special Projects Delivery: Support priority initiatives (e.g., cost savings, process optimization etc.) through targeted data analysis.
Process & Reporting Improvement: Identify opportunities to automate, standardize, and improve data flows and reporting processes.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Finance, Laboratory Operations, and Digital & Data teams to define requirements and deliver insights aligned to organizational priorities.
Business Analysis and Decision Support: Partner with operational leaders and business unit to analyze volume trends, performance metrics, and business data, providing actionable insights that support informed decision-making and operational improvements.
Provides financial analysis and reporting for assigned programs/departments including advising and supporting the development of forecasts, preparing monthly variance analysis and commentary on spending.
Leads/Develops cost/benefit analyses and business cases for operational scenarios/special projects.
Other duties or projects as assigned.
Education and Experience-
Bachelor’s degree in Finance/ Business or a related field.
5–7 years of experience in data analysis, preferably within healthcare, public sector, or complex operational environments.
Advanced Excel including data manipulation, Power Query, and data modeling is required.
Experience with Power BI or similar visualization tools is preferred.
Working knowledge of SQL is considered an asset.
Knowledge and Skills-
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with ability to work through complex and ambiguous datasets.
Ability to translate clinical and operational data into financial and strategic insights.
Strong communication skills with ability to present insights to non-technical and executive audiences.
High attention to detail and data integrity.
Oral communication and interpersonal skills, to provide technical advice and guidance to peers and liaise with all levels of internal and external stakeholders/contacts.
Written communication skills to prepare commentary on analyses develop and deliver presentations, training documents and procedural guidelines
.
Attributes and Competencies-
Works independently to structure analyses, validate data, and develop insights to support decision-making. Exercises judgment in interpreting data, identifying risks and issues, and recommending solutions to support Finance and operational leadership.
Identifies and summarizes program/department current month and year-to-date variances and forecast issues and provides resolution to related issues.
Prepares and reviews cost benefits analyses and business cases on various operational scenarios/ special projects to make recommendations to support management financial decision making.
Ensures cost centre managers understand their financial reports in support of the financial management of their respective cost centres
.
